html:
The Austronesians are the peoples who speak Austronesian languages. The map shows them in the islands of Southeast Asia from 3000 to 400 BCE, as they spread out by sea from their homeland in Taiwan.

They were farmers and sailors. With outrigger canoes and sails they carried rice, pigs, pottery and their languages south. They reached the Philippines around 2200 BCE, then moved on to Borneo, Sulawesi, Java, Sumatra and the coast of mainland Southeast Asia, where the Cham later built their kingdom. Taiwan jade moved along their routes in the Maritime Jade Road.

From about 1600 BCE the Lapita carried Austronesian culture into the open Pacific, and their descendants the Polynesians went as far as Hawaii and New Zealand. Westward, Austronesian sailors settled Madagascar in the first millennium CE. Before 1500 no language family had spread over more of the globe.
